title: Toward Guarantees for Clinical Reasoning in Vision Language Models via Formal Verification
abstract: arXiv:2602.24111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) show promise in drafting radiology reports, yet they frequently suffer from logical inconsistencies, generating diagnostic impressions unsupported by their own perceptual findings or missing logically entailed conclusions. Standard lexical metrics heavily penalize clinical paraphrasing and fail to capture these deductive failures in reference-free settings. Toward guarantees for clinical reasoning, we introduce a neurosymbolic verification framework that deterministically audits the internal consistency of VLM-generated reports. Our pipeline autoformalizes free-text radiographic findings into structured propositional evidence, utilizing an SMT solver (Z3) and a clinical knowledge base to verify whether each diagnostic claim is mathematically entailed, hallucinated, or omitted. translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）在起草放射学报告方面展现出前景，但它们经常出现逻辑不一致的问题，即生成其自身感知发现所不支持的诊断印象，或遗漏逻辑上必然得出的结论。标准词汇指标严重惩罚临床释义，且在无参考设置下无法捕获这些演绎推理失败。为实现临床推理的可靠性保证，我们引入了一个神经符号验证框架，该框架能够确定性地审计VLM生成报告的内部一致性。我们的流程将自由文本的放射学发现自动形式化为结构化命题证据，利用SMT求解器（Z3）和临床知识库来验证每个诊断声明是在数学上被蕴含、属于幻觉，还是被遗漏。在五个胸部X光基准上对七个VLM进行评估，我们的验证器揭示了不同的推理失败模式，例如……
tldr: 本文提出一个神经符号验证框架，利用SMT求解器（Z3）和临床知识库将放射学报告自动形式化为命题证据，从而确定性地审计视觉语言模型生成报告的内部一致性，检测诊断声明是被数学蕴含、产生幻觉还是被遗漏。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a neurosymbolic verification framework that autoformalizes radiology report findings into propositional evidence using an SMT solver (Z3) and clinical knowledge base, enabling deterministic auditing of VLM-generated reports to detect whether diagnostic claims are mathematically entailed, hallucinated, or omitted.
